title: The Chief Series of A₄, Explicitly
content: The parent proves A₄ solvable indirectly. This file exhibits the classical chief (solvable) series A₄ ▷ V₄ ▷ {e} and identifies both factors with standard models — A₄/V₄ ≅ ℤ/3ℤ and V₄ ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)². (This is a chief, not a composition, series: V₄ ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)² is not simple; the true composition series refines it to A₄ ▷ V₄ ▷ C₂ ▷ 1.) V₄ is Mathlib's alternatingGroup.kleinFour (Fin 4), the subgroup generated by the (2,2)-cycle-type permutations. card_fin_four proves Nat.card (Fin 4) = 4, the hypothesis every Klein-four lemma requires.

title: V₄ ◁ A₄ and V₄ = [A₄, A₄]
content: v4_normal (from normal_kleinFour) makes V₄ a normal subgroup — it is the unique Sylow 2-subgroup, hence even characteristic — so A₄/V₄ is a genuine quotient group; the instance v4_normal_inst registers this so the group structure is available already at statement-elaboration time in the ≃* theorems below. v4_eq_commutator records that V₄ equals the commutator subgroup [A₄, A₄], so the exhibited chain is exactly the derived series of A₄ — the two standard descriptions of A₄'s solvability coincide.

title: The Factor Orders: 12 = 3 · 4
content: card_a4 gives |A₄| = 4!/2 = 12, card_v4 gives |V₄| = 4, and card_quotient derives |A₄/V₄| = 3 from Lagrange's theorem (Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_subgroup: |G| = |G/H|·|H|). These are the orders of the chief-series layers, and the prime factorization 12 = 2²·3 foreshadows the factor structure (ℤ/2ℤ)² and ℤ/3ℤ.

title: Top Factor: A₄/V₄ ≅ ℤ/3ℤ
content: quotient_iso_zmod3 identifies the top chief factor (A₄/V₄, which is simple). The quotient has prime order 3, so isCyclic_of_prime_card makes it cyclic, and mulEquivOfPrimeCardEq (two groups of the same prime order are isomorphic) produces the explicit isomorphism to Multiplicative (ZMod 3) — no generator needs to be exhibited by hand. card_mult_zmod3 supplies the matching |Multiplicative (ZMod 3)| = 3.

title: Bottom Factor V₄ ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)² and the Packaged Series
content: v4_iso_zmod2_sq identifies the bottom factor: V₄ is a Klein four-group (kleinFour_isKleinFour: order 4, exponent 2), and IsKleinFour.nonempty_mulEquiv says any two Klein four-groups are isomorphic, giving V₄ ≅ Multiplicative (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) with no element matching. composition_series_A4 bundles the full answer to the open question: V₄ normal, both factor orders (3 and 4), and both factor isomorphisms (ℤ/3ℤ and (ℤ/2ℤ)²). Both factors abelian ⟹ A₄ solvable, constructively.
mathContext: $V_4 \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$; the packaged series has abelian factors $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ and $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$.
prerequisites: the Klein four-group as order-4 exponent-2
